lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 4, what did Shang China write on bones and shells? (Early Chinese characters.) Japan later borrowed China's characters to write its own language. Today: medieval Japan.
Japan is a chain of islands with steep mountains, so people grew rice in the narrow valleys and plains. From 794 its emperors lived in a new capital, Heian-kyo, now called Kyoto.

At the emperor's court, nobles wrote poems and diaries. About 1010 a court lady, Murasaki Shikibu, finished The Tale of Genji, one of the world's first novels. Writers mixed Chinese characters with Japanese sound signs called kana.
Far from the court, lords kept warriors called samurai. They fought on horseback, were expected to be loyal to their lord and brave, and often learned poetry and calligraphy too.

In 1192 the emperor gave the warrior leader Minamoto Yoritomo the title shogun. From then on, shoguns ran the country for hundreds of years, while the emperor stayed on the throne as its highest figure.

In 1274 and 1281 Kublai Khan, the Mongol ruler of China, sent great fleets to invade. Both times samurai defended the coast and storms wrecked the ships. The Japanese called the storms the divine wind.

Calligraphy is writing with a brush and ink, each stroke in the right order. Zen Buddhist temples made rock gardens of raked gravel and stones, such as the one at Ryoan-ji in Kyoto, for calm thinking.
Try it in the world: build a quiet garden of raked sand with a few big stones and a small bridge. Add a wooden house with sliding doors. Next: the Aztecs and the Incas.

exercises.explain: Samurai were warriors who served a lord.

exercises.prompt: Who wrote The Tale of Genji?
exercises.hint: She was a lady at the emperor's court.

exercises.prompt: Japan is a chain of islands.
exercises.hint: Look at a map east of China.
exercises.explain: True: Japan is a chain of islands with steep mountains.

choices: beautiful writing with a brush and ink
exercises.explain: Beautiful writing with a brush and ink.

exercises.prompt: Which city became Japan's capital in 794?
The Tale of Genji was finished about 1010. Yoritomo became shogun in 1192. About how many years later was that?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Two are warriors; one is about writing.
exercises.explain: Shogun: the top warrior ruler. Samurai: a warrior. Kana: sound signs. Emperor: the highest figure on the throne.

exercises.prompt: What stopped the Mongol fleets in 1274 and 1281?
exercises.hint: The Japanese gave the storms a special name.
choices: storms, and samurai on the coast
the fleets got lost in fog
exercises.explain: Samurai defended the coast, and storms wrecked the fleets both times.

exercises.prompt: After 1192, the emperor ran the army and the government.
exercises.explain: False: the shogun ran the country; the emperor stayed on the throne as its highest figure.

exercises.prompt: What were Zen rock gardens made for?
exercises.hint: They are quiet places of gravel and stones.
exercises.explain: For calm thinking, in Zen Buddhist temples.

exercises.prompt: Why did Japan borrow Chinese characters?
exercises.hint: Think of how writing reached Japan.
choices: Japan had no writing of its own before
exercises.explain: Japan had no writing system of its own, so it borrowed China's characters and later added kana.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, earliest first.
exercises.hint: Look at the years: the smaller the year, the earlier.

exercises.prompt: Why did most people in medieval Japan live in valleys and plains?
choices: the mountains were too steep to farm
exercises.explain: Most of Japan is steep mountains, so people farmed rice on the flat land in valleys and plains.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: part of court life, or of the samurai's world?
exercises.hint: The court was the emperor's; samurai served lords and shoguns.
exercises.explain: Court life: poems, diaries and The Tale of Genji. Samurai: loyalty to a lord, fighting on horseback, serving a shogun.

exercises.prompt: Samurai were expected to learn poetry and calligraphy as well as fighting.
exercises.hint: Look back at the samurai card.
exercises.explain: True: many samurai learned poetry and calligraphy too.

exercises.prompt: Match each name to what it is known for.
exercises.hint: A writer, a warrior leader, a Mongol ruler and a temple.
exercises.explain: Murasaki Shikibu wrote The Tale of Genji. Minamoto Yoritomo became shogun in 1192. Kublai Khan sent fleets to invade in 1274 and 1281. Ryoan-ji in Kyoto has a famous Zen rock garden.
